requirement:
For a response with exactly one `submit_result` call, arguments other than an
object containing only the `result` field end the request with
`ValidationError::Agent`. Decoding the field's value into `R` follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission.decoding`.
rationale:
Obligation: for a response with exactly one `submit_result` call, arguments other than an object containing only `result` must end the request with `ValidationError::Agent`. Decoding the result into `R` is delegated to the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission.decoding`.

Coverage:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#mod[submission_tests]/fn[submission_envelopes_require_one_result_field]` checks the envelope check directly. It rejects null, array, string, boolean, `{}`, `{"other":true}` and `{"result":true,"extra":false}`, and asserts the error message "submit_result requires exactly result". It also asserts that a `result` of any shape is accepted and returned unchanged.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[typed_submission_references_resolve_and_invalid_results_are_agent_errors]` runs the whole path. It sends the invalid argument objects `{}`, `{"other":true}` and `{"result":true,"extra":true}`, plus the undecodable `{"result":"wrong"}`. Each case asserts `Err(ValidationError::Agent(_))`, and the vetting callback panics if it is reached. This covers the missing-field, wrong-field and extra-field cases end to end. It also covers the decoding-failure case that the cited requirement governs, in the subject's setting.

The non-object argument cases (null, array, string, boolean) are checked only at the unit level. This is acceptable because `converse` in `agent.rs` builds `arguments` as `Value::Object(...)` from the call's argument map, and it passes any `submitted_value` error down the same error path. The end-to-end test therefore exercises the mapping to `ValidationError::Agent`, and the unit test exercises each rejected shape.

I found no gap.
